title: Smallest Palindromic Rearrangement I
statement:
The input string `s` is itself a palindrome: it reads the same from left to right and from right to left.

Rearrange the letters of `s` (every letter used exactly as many times as it occurs in `s`) so that the result is again a palindrome. Of all the palindromes that can be made this way, return the one that comes first in dictionary (lexicographic) order.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

A palindrome is fixed by its left half and, when its length is odd, its middle letter: the right half is the left half reversed. So every letter puts exactly half of its copies into the left half. Strings are compared from the left, so the smallest palindrome has the smallest possible left half, which is those half-copies in ascending order. Counting the 26 letters builds that sorted half directly; trying every permutation would take factorial time.

## Approach

1. Count every letter of `s` in `counts` (index 0 for `a` up to 25 for `z`).
2. Walk the letters from `a` to `z` and append `Math.floor(counts[letter] / 2)` copies of each to `half`.
3. A letter with an odd count can only stand in the middle. Because `s` is a palindrome there is at most one such letter, and only when the length is odd; keep it in `middle`.
4. Return `half + middle + mirrored`, where `mirrored` is `half` reversed.

## Example 1, step by step

For `s = "z"`, counting gives `counts[25] = 1` and zero for every other letter. At `z`, `Math.floor(1 / 2) = 0` copies go into `half`, and the odd count sets `middle = "z"`. With `half = ""` and `mirrored = ""`, the answer is `"z"`.

Example 3 shows more: `"daccad"` has two each of `a`, `c` and `d`, so `half = "acd"`, there is no middle letter, and the answer is `"acd" + "dca" = "acddca"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one counting pass, 26 alphabet steps, and building the answer of length n.
- Space: O(n) for the answer; `counts` has a fixed 26 entries.

## Pitfalls

- The odd letter must stay in the middle even when it is the smallest letter: in `"bab"` the single `a` cannot come first, so the answer is `"bab"`.
- Each side gets half of a letter's copies; appending the full count would double the string.
- Sorting the whole string does not give a palindrome (`"babab"` would become `"aabbb"`); sort only the half, then mirror it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `counts[letter]` | how many times the letter with index `letter` occurs in `s` |
| `ch` | the letter itself, `a` to `z` |
| `half` | left half of the answer, in ascending order |
| `middle` | the letter with an odd count, or `""` |
| `mirrored` | `half` reversed: the right half of the answer |

narration.2: One counter per lowercase letter, index 0 for a up to 25 for z.
narration.4: ...and add one to that letter's counter.
narration.6: half will hold the left half of the answer.
narration.7: middle will hold the letter with an odd count, if there is one.
narration.8: Go through the alphabet in order, so half comes out sorted.
narration.10: Half of this letter's copies belong to the left half; the other half mirror them on the right.
narration.11: An odd count leaves one copy over...
narration.12: ...and that copy can only stand in the middle.
narration.15: The right half is the left half read backwards.
narration.16: Join the sorted left half, the middle letter and the mirrored right half.
